citation: J. Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, 2018. Chapter 1, especially the operator–vector correspondence and Schmidt decomposition.
role: Standard mathematical context for vectorization, singular values, partial traces, and product vectors; no additional BFG premise.

citation: A. Einstein, B. Podolsky, and N. Rosen, “Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?”, Physical Review 47, 777–780 (1935).
role: Historical context for correlated separated systems and the completeness question.

citation: E. Schrödinger, “Discussion of Probability Relations between Separated Systems”, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 31(4), 555–563 (1935).
role: Historical discussion of joint state descriptions and matched observables; not a derivation of BFG rule R3.

citation: J. S. Bell, “On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen paradox”, Physics Physique Fizika 1, 195–200 (1964).
role: Original Bell theorem and the incompatibility of local hidden-variable descriptions with all quantum correlations.

citation: J. F. Clauser, M. A. Horne, A. Shimony, and R. A. Holt, “Proposed Experiment to Test Local Hidden-Variable Theories”, Physical Review Letters 23, 880–884 (1969).
role: Experimental Bell correlation inequality; the local bound concerns outcome statistics.

citation: B. S. Cirel’son, “Quantum generalizations of Bell’s inequality”, Letters in Mathematical Physics 4, 93–100 (1980).
role: Quantum bounds on Bell correlations, including the standard CHSH bound 2√2; comparison only.

citation: R. F. Werner, “Quantum states with Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen correlations admitting a hidden-variable model”, Physical Review A 40, 4277–4281 (1989).
role: Distinguishes mixed-state entanglement from Bell nonlocality; projective-measurement local models need not imply separability.

citation: A. M. Gleason, “Measures on the Closed Subspaces of a Hilbert Space”, Journal of Mathematics and Mechanics 6(6), 885–893 (1957).
role: Trace-form representation under nonnegative orthogonally additive measures on subspaces, for Hilbert-space dimension at least three.

citation: P. Busch, “Quantum States and Generalized Observables: A Simple Proof of Gleason’s Theorem”, Physical Review Letters 91, 120403 (2003).
role: Generalized effect-space probability theorem, including dimension two; requires additional probability and effect assumptions.

citation: B. Hensen et al., “Loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins separated by 1.3 kilometres”, Nature 526, 682–686 (2015).
role: Experimental example with event-ready preparation and treatment of detection and locality loopholes; not an empirical BFG test.

citation: C. Marletto and V. Vedral, “Gravitationally Induced Entanglement between Two Massive Particles is Sufficient Evidence of Quantum Effects in Gravity”, Physical Review Letters 119, 240402 (2017).
role: Conditional comparison for a physical mediator: local coupling of each quantum endpoint to the mediator, with no direct endpoint interaction.
